newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa counts cost of worker protests.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa counts cost of worker protests.

text.p: Deutsche Lufthansa AG said on Tuesday that a two hour protest strike organised on Monday by the DAG white-collar employees trade union resulted in loss of business "in the millions (of marks)".

In a letter to customers published as a full-page advertisement in major German newspapers, Lufthansa chairman Juergen Weber criticised the protest, which led to the cancellation of 35 Lufthansa flights, as "unjustified".
"It also goes against the efforts of the thousands of employees who are ready, by giving their support, to strengthen Lufthansa's competitiveness and make jobs secure," Weber said.
Weber had already published a similar full-page letter on Friday reassuring customers that it would do all it could to overcome any disruption that should occur.

Lufthansa concluded a wage deal with the transport and public sector employees represented by the OeTV union in October. Talks broke down with DAG when it failed to agree the union's four percent pay increase demand.
DAG agreed on Monday to hold further talks with Lufthansa on November 19.
